DeGennaro explained that the moratorium would still be in place until June 12, so if the board wanted to make that change, there is certainly time to do so. ... Ultimately, the commissioners approved the draft data center ordinance ... and lifted the moratorium.

decisions.notes: This LaGrange Daily News article does not carry an on-page publication date in the archived text; it corroborates the prior 'around May 8, 2026' estimate and, via the county attorney's June 12, 2026 reference, is consistent with the vote occurring in the weeks before that date.

duration.from: 30 days; county announced plan to consider a further 180-day extension after an August 6 public hearing
duration.to: Original 30 days (2026-07-09 to approximately 2026-08-08); the Board of Commissioners voted unanimously on Aug. 6, 2026 to extend the moratorium 180 days, through Feb. 2, 2027, and to establish a Data Center Development Standards Study Committee, which the Board asked to complete its work by Dec. 4, 2026.
duration.reason: Walker County's own local newspaper coverage (Discover Walker) and the Chattanooga Times Free Press both confirm the Board voted at its Aug. 6, 2026 meeting ('last Thursday' per the Aug. 10 Discover Walker article) to extend the moratorium 180 days, with an explicit new end date of Feb. 2, 2027, superseding the prior CSV text that only described the extension as 'announced' rather than adopted.

current_end_date_iso.reason: Discover Walker's Aug. 10, 2026 article states directly: 'The moratorium applies only to unincorporated areas of Walker County and will remain in effect until February 2, 2027,' repeated later in the same article as the operative end date.

current_status.from: The documented 30-day moratorium expired on approximately 2026-08-08. Walker County's official July notice said the Board would consider a 180-day extension after a public hearing; no adopted extension instrument was located in the County's published materials reviewed through 2026-08-19. [VERIFY: signed resolution or later extension record not located]
current_status.to: Extended and active as of 2026-09-23. The Board of Commissioners voted unanimously at its Aug. 6, 2026 meeting to extend the data center moratorium 180 days, through Feb. 2, 2027, and created a Data Center Development Standards Study Committee (chaired by the Economic Development Director, vice-chaired by the Planning Director, with two members per district commissioner plus the Chamber of Commerce president), tasked to complete its work by Dec. 4, 2026. The moratorium applies only to unincorporated Walker County; municipalities within the county must act separately. No data center companies had been named as interested parties as of the extension vote.
current_status.reason: Resolves the VERIFY marker: the extension was in fact adopted (not merely proposed) at the Aug. 6, 2026 meeting, confirmed by both the Chattanooga Times Free Press and Discover Walker, correcting the prior record's premature 'expired' determination.

verify_resolutions.marker: [VERIFY: signed resolution or later extension record not located]
verify_resolutions.note: Located two independent local news accounts (Chattanooga Times Free Press and Discover Walker) of the Aug. 6, 2026 Board of Commissioners meeting confirming the unanimous vote extending the moratorium 180 days through Feb. 2, 2027, and establishing a study committee. No numbered resolution/ordinance identifier was located, but the extension's adoption itself is now confirmed by two independent sources.

evidence.title: Walker County extends data center moratorium by 180 days, creates study group
evidence.supports: Confirms the Board of Commissioners voted unanimously to extend the moratorium by 180 days and create an impact study group.
evidence.quote: The Walker County Board of Commissioners voted unanimously Thursday to extend the county's data center moratorium by 180 days and create an impact study group.

evidence.title: Walker County Extends Data Center Moratorium, Creates Study Committee
evidence.supports: Confirms the extension's specific new end date (Feb. 2, 2027), that it applies only to unincorporated areas, and details of the newly formed study committee and its Dec. 4, 2026 deadline.
evidence.quote: Commissioners approved the extension at last Thursday's commission meeting. The moratorium applies only to unincorporated areas of Walker County and will remain in effect until February 2, 2027. ... The Board of Commissioners has asked the committee to complete its work by December 4, 2026.

decisions.notes: The prior record's 'expired' determination was premature: the county adopted the 180-day extension it had only announced as under consideration, before the original 30-day term lapsed. duration_days is left at the original '30' per the existing convention in this dataset (e.g., Bulloch, DeKalb) of keeping the initial fixed term while current_end_date_iso tracks the latest operative extension date.
